# AI Notes

## Which parts were AI-generated vs. written by me

### AI-generated (via Kiro / Claude)

**Backend** (`src/models.py`, `src/storage.py`, `src/main.py`, `tests/test_api.py`,
`requirements.txt`, initial `README.md`) — the full initial implementation was
generated from the assignment brief in a single session.

**Frontend** (`frontend/index.html`) — the single-page web UI was generated by the
AI based on my prompt: "build a polished, dark-theme SPA using only vanilla
HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, that talks to the FastAPI backend."

### My contributions

- Reviewed every file line by line before accepting it.
- Ran the full test suite (`pytest`) and the live server myself on a clean checkout,
  and verified all endpoints manually with `curl` and the browser.
- Decided to add the **search bonus** (`?search=` query param on `GET /expenses`):
  I added the one-liner filter in `storage.py` and wired the `search` param into
  `main.py`. The AI generated the plumbing after I asked for it; I checked the
  logic and added a test case by hand.
- Added CORS middleware and the `aiofiles` dependency (needed for FastAPI's
  `StaticFiles`) after the AI's initial version didn't include them — the server
  threw a `RuntimeError` on startup without `aiofiles`, which I caught during
  local testing.
- Tweaked the frontend colour palette and layout column widths to my taste after
  seeing the first render.

---

## What I validated / tested

- **`pytest` — all tests pass** covering: add + id increment, validation errors
  (negative/zero amount, blank fields, invalid date, missing field), list,
  category filter (including case-insensitivity and "no match"), single-item
  fetch (200 + 404), totals summary (populated + empty store), delete (success,
  404, and totals updating after delete).
- **Live manual testing** — started the server with `uvicorn src.main:app --reload`,
  opened the browser at `http://127.0.0.1:8000`, and exercised every UI action:
  - Added expenses across different categories
  - Filtered by category from the dropdown
  - Searched by title keyword
  - Checked the totals stats bar and category breakdown updated in real time
  - Deleted an expense and confirmed it disappeared and the total updated
- **Persistence** — killed and restarted the server; confirmed existing expenses
  were still there (loaded from `data/expenses.json`).
- **Search endpoint** — verified `?search=coffee` returned only matching titles,
  case-insensitively; verified `?category=Food&search=latte` combined both filters.

---

## Design choices worth calling out

- **Search bonus chosen over monthly summary / Docker** — search is immediately
  useful in the UI (the search box is front-and-centre), and the implementation
  was a clean one-liner that composed well with the existing category filter. A
  monthly summary endpoint was tempting but would have required date-parsing logic
  that added complexity without adding much to the reviewer experience.
- **Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS frontend** — I explicitly asked the AI to avoid React,
  Vue, or any build tooling. A bundled SPA would need `npm install` and a build
  step, which complicates the "install and run" story in the README. A single
  `index.html` served by FastAPI itself means the reviewer runs one command and
  gets both the API and the UI.
- **StaticFiles + FileResponse root** — FastAPI's `StaticFiles` serves
  `frontend/index.html` as a static asset at `/static/index.html`, but I also
  added a `GET /` route that returns it via `FileResponse` so the root URL loads
  the UI directly. The AI's first draft only mounted `StaticFiles` without the
  root route; I added the `FileResponse` handler after noticing `GET /` returned
  a JSON health object instead of the page.
- **CORS `allow_origins=["*"]`** — fine for a local dev assignment; in production
  this would be locked to the frontend's specific origin.

---

## AI suggestions I decided not to use

- **Docker support** — the AI offered a `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml`.
  I skipped it because the assignment says "Data can be stored in memory or a
  local JSON file; no database is required", and Docker adds reviewer friction
  (they need Docker installed). A plain `pip install + uvicorn` run is simpler
  and matches the assignment's spirit.
- **SQLite backend** — the AI mentioned SQLite as "more production-realistic"
  than a JSON file. I kept the JSON file approach because it matches the
  assignment spec exactly and avoids pulling in SQLAlchemy or another ORM.
- **React/Vue frontend** — the AI offered to scaffold a React app. I declined
  because it would have introduced a `node_modules` tree and a build step, making
  the reviewer setup more complex than the assignment warrants.
- **`append-only` log storage** — the AI noted that rewriting the full JSON on
  every change is inefficient at scale. True, but at the scale of a personal
  expense tracker (hundreds of records at most) it's a non-issue, and the simpler
  read-modify-write-all approach is much easier to reason about and debug.
